newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algerian family were bomb victims -- newspaper.
newsitem.headline: Algerian family were bomb victims -- newspaper.

text.p: An Algerian man, his pregnant wife and their daughter were killed in their beds in a bomb blast in the northern Algerian town of Lakhdaria on Monday night, a local newspaper reported on Wednesday, revealing details of the blast.

"It was around 3 a.m.. Two bombs were placed either side of the building. The most powerful was against the outside wall of a bedroom, just near the head of the bed where the parents were sleeping," the independent newspaper Liberte quoted a witness as saying.

"The explosion practically destroyed the first floor of the three-storey building. The father, his wife and their daughter died on the spot. The mother, nine months pregnant, was, like her husband, blown to pieces."
Only the family's six-year-old boy survived. He was blown into the road.
The newspaper did not indicate why the family was targeted or whether the bombing was simply indiscriminate.

The security forces, in a statement on the official news agency APS, reported the blast and a death toll of three on Tuesday but gave no details of the attack which was believed to be the work of Moslem fundamentalists trying to overthrow the government.
A government-appointed body last August said 1,400 people had been killed by bombs, blamed on Moslem fundamentalists, in the past two years.
At least 50,000 people have been killed since violence erupted after the authorities in January 1992 cancelled a general election in which Islamists had taken a commanding lead.
